newsitem.title: UK: NatWest joins ScotAm bidding - paper.
newsitem.headline: NatWest joins ScotAm bidding - paper.

text.p: National Westminster Bank has emerged as a last minute bidder for British mutual insurer Scottish Amicable, the Independent on Sunday newspaper said.
The bank has signed a confidentiality agreement to gain access to the information it needs to frame a bid which must be submitted by Friday, it said.
Five other suitors have signed confidentiality agreements. They are Fortis Amev, GE Capital, Abbey National, Prudential Corp Plc and Australian Mutual Provident, the paper added.
The company sparked takeover interest last month when it announced it was planning to shed its mutual status and seek a stock market flotation.
Abbey National made an initial bid worth about 1.4 billion pounds ($2.25 billion) which was followed by a 1.9 billion pound offer from the Prudential a few days later.

On February 11 the mutual said it would take independent professional advice during the selection process, adding its objectives was to maximise financial benefits for with-profits policy holders "taking into account both short-term and long-term returns".
